records.source: definition: "Operationalizing equity is the ongoing, participatory practice of making equity a concrete part of how work is designed, decided, resourced, carried out and reviewed. It means identifying and changing policies, procedures, practices and power relationships that create avoidable barriers or unequal opportunities, and learning with the people affected whether those changes improve access, participation and outcomes."

    "What decision, process or practice is open to change, and who can influence it?",
    "Who experiences its benefits, burdens and barriers differently, and what history or structural conditions help explain that?",
    "Whose knowledge is missing, and how can affected people shape the problem and options while choices remain open?",
    "What do available evidence and lived experience establish, and what remains unknown?",
    "Which alternatives change the underlying barrier or distribution of opportunity, resources and influence?",

    "What will change in the actual work, and who has agreed responsibility for carrying it forward?",
    "How will people learn what happened to their input, examine effects and decide whether to retain, revise or stop the approach?",

      { title: "DHS equity policy", href: "/equity-policy", description: "Read the policy context for considering equity in workforce, policy, program, and service decisions." },

records.source:
commitments: [
    { name: "Antiracist", body: "Racial equity is defined as measurable change in the lives of people of color: an outcome in the work, not a values paragraph." },
    { name: "Multicultural", body: "Programs, notices, and channels are built for the languages, households, and communities that actually use them." },
    { name: "Intercultural", body: "Staff can see who a process was built for, in language, disability, culture, nationhood, and place, and change the work when it does not reach them." },
  ]

changes.before: Racial equity is defined as measurable change in the lives of people of color: an outcome in the work, not a values paragraph.
changes.sourceLiteral: "Racial equity is defined as measurable change in the lives of people of color: an outcome in the work, not a values paragraph."
changes.reason: Restore fuller policy definition rather than equating racial equity with any measurable change.
changes.after: The policy connects racial equity with eliminating racial disparities, improving outcomes for everyone and changing systems with measurable effects in the lives of people of color.

changes.before: Programs, notices, and channels are built for the languages, households, and communities that actually use them.
changes.sourceLiteral: "Programs, notices, and channels are built for the languages, households, and communities that actually use them."
changes.reason: Separate policy definition from program-authored application; do not imply current services already meet aspiration.
changes.after: Multicultural settings include people from different cultures. In service design, ask whether programs, notices and channels work for the people who use them.

changes.before: Staff can see who a process was built for, in language, disability, culture, nationhood, and place, and change the work when it does not reach them.
changes.sourceLiteral: "Staff can see who a process was built for, in language, disability, culture, nationhood, and place, and change the work when it does not reach them."
changes.reason: Match policy distinction: engagement and adaptation, not merely identifying exclusion.
changes.after: Intercultural practice involves engaging across cultures, understanding differences and commonalities, and adapting. Ask whose perspective shaped a process and what people need to use it.
